decision.title: The book's story is Vane, a feature-flag service (packet book-14)

body.p: , after . The owner rejected the Latch story (door locks, a controller and its services: "nobody thinks of doors") and chose a feature-flag service, something developers know. The five projects of stay; only the story and its names change.

item.p: Vane: an SDK asks the evaluation service (flag-service) about flags; the service keeps flags, targeting rules and percentages in flag-registry (PostgreSQL) and flag-cache (Redis); owners roll flags out by percentage, the service checks guardrail metrics, pauses a flag after three failed checks, and has a kill switch; an audit-service records changes. The name is short, neutral and no feature-flag product we know of.

Same structure, new names: every count, order, flaw and diff the chapters rely on is kept (docs/tasks/book.md sections 2 and 8): the draft's 12 BCP 14 paragraphs with one unanchored SHOULD and anchors out of document order, the -00/-01 changes ("five" to "three", "one minute" to "five minutes"), 11 xrefs, 4 terms, RFC 2119/5234/8174 and RFC 6238 (kept: a one-time password before a rollout; M'Raihi keeps the collation lesson); the machine's graph and its four flaws (archived unreachable, flag.evaluated undeclared, flag.archived unused, status.response only sent); the services diagram's layout; the call-chain change (listFlags N+1 over registry.getFlag, killFlag drops cache.getFlag and adds audit.record: "1 -> 1 + n"); the traces' 16 and 30 spans and five-row diff.

Files renamed: latch.xml, latch-00.xml, latch.xsd to vane.*; lock.scxml to flag.scxml; latch-data.xsd to vane-data.xsd (namespace urn:example:vane); doors.ts to flags.ts; the symlinks to them with them.

Chapters follow mechanically: packets book-15 to book-21 own the files of book-6 to book-12, apply the rename table, regenerate every example output with --update and make the prose match what the outputs say; book-13 integrates last. The book never mentions Latch.
